This compound is predicted to interact with Npc172494, which is known to target the EP4 subtype of the prostaglandin E2 receptor. The evidence is supported by a final score of 0.5635, indicating a moderate level of confidence in the relationship. The mechanism involves a cascade where the compound acts as a target of Npc172494, which in turn modulates the EP4 receptor. The integration of these pathways suggests that the compound may exert its effects through a receptor-mediated mechanism, potentially influencing signaling pathways related to inflammation or cell proliferation. The evidence is consistent with a mechanistic link, though further validation through experimental studies would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction and functional role of the compound in this context.
